;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Syrian Civil War]]:
**Syria's political opposition urges [[United States|US]] action in response to the Syrian government's [[barrel bomb|barrel bombing]] campaign in the city of [[Aleppo]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/2014/04/14/us-syria-crisis-letter-idUSBREA3D1AO20140414 (Reuters)]
**[[Syrian Army|Syrian government troops]] recapture the towns of [[Al-Sarkha (Bakhah)|Al-Sarkha]] and [[Ma'loula]] near the [[Syria]]-[[Lebanon]] border. [http://www.dailystar.com.lb/News/Middle-East/2014/Apr-14/253263-syria-army-retakes-maaloula-security-source.ashx#axzz2yrph206W (''The Daily Star'')]
*Two [[Abu Sayyaf]] militants are killed and several captured in a raid in the [[Philippines]] city of [[Zamboanga City|Zamboanga]]. [http://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/abu-sayyaf-militants-killed-philippine-raid-23313423 (AP via ABC News)]
*[[Islamist insurgency in Nigeria]]
**Twin bomb blasts [[April 2014 Abuja bombing|hit a crowded bus station]] at the outskirts of the [[Nigeria]]n capital [[Abuja]], killing at least 71 and injuring more than 120 others. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-africa-27018751 (BBC)] [http://www.aljazeera.com/news/africa/2014/04/bus-station-bombed-abuja-rush-hour-20144147323279272.html (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2014 pro-Russian protests in Ukraine]]
**Pro-Russian gunmen storm another police station, in the town of [[Horlivka]], [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-27018199 (BBC News)]

;Arts and culture
*The ''[[Washington Post]]'' and ''[[The Guardian]]'' newspapers win the [[Pulitzer Prize for Public Service]] for their stories on the [[National Security Agency]] based on leaks from [[Edward Snowden]]. [http://www.sltrib.com/sltrib/world/57817436-68/reporting-public-post-pulitzer.html.csp (AP via ''Salt Lake Tribune'')]

;Business and economy
*[[United States|American]] financial services company [[TIAA–CREF]] agrees to buy [[Nuveen Investments]] for [[American dollar|$]]6.25 billion. [http://online.wsj.com/article/BT-CO-20140414-704535.html (''Wall Street Journal'')]

;Law and crime
*Radical British Muslim cleric [[Abu Hamza al-Masri]] goes on trial in the American state of [[New York (state)|New York]] for 11 alleged terrorism offenses. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-27015350# (BBC News)]
*A [[United States Court of Appeals for the Third Circuit|United States court]] overturns the conviction of Andrew Auernheimer (known as [[weev]]), who was sentenced to 41-months in prison in 2010 for hacking the [[AT&T]] website, stealing millions of [[iPad]] user e-mails. [http://www.pcworld.com/article/2143180/atandt-hacker-weev-released-from-prison-after-appeals-court-overturns-conviction.html (PC World)]

;Politics and elections
*Voters in the [[Republic of Macedonia]] head to the polls for a [[Macedonian general election, 2014|runoff presidential election]]. [http://www.voanews.com/content/macedonia-heads-for-presidential-runoff-vote/1892621.html (Voice of America)]
*[[Vietnam]] frees [[Nguyen Tien Trung]] and [[Vi Duc Hoi]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-27019624 (BBC News)]
